To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) symbolic model checking can be applied to the verification of state/event models; (b) symbolic model checking of large systems can be made practical by using compositionality and dependency information; and (c) the resulting tool can be used to verify industrial designs.
the compositionality and dependency techniques can reduce the state space of a large state/event model by 2 to 5 orders of magnitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to verify a system that is described as a composition of many concurrent state/event models.
improving the efficiency of symbolic state/event model checking.
the development of efficient symbolic model checking techniques for large state/event systems.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of symbolic state/event model checking can be improved by a factor of more than 10000 by using compositionality and dependency reduction.
the use of compositionality and dependency can be used to significantly reduce the state space size and thus the time and memory requirements for model checking.
the use of compositionality and dependency information is essential for verification of large state/event models.
